atomicity.reason: One obligation (return the state of charge of the winning slot at initialisation); the neither-valid sentence is an edge case of the same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: Self-contained: both slots, the checksum verification, the selection criterion and the failure report are all stated.

feasibility.reason: Reading two slots and comparing checksums and counters at initialisation is trivial and consistent with the write requirement.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_SOC_STORE states it hands the higher-counter valid slot to the corrector on wake-up; this requirement specifies that selection including the checksum verification.

unambiguity.reason: 'whichever checksum-valid slot carries the higher write counter' has no defined outcome when both valid slots carry equal counters, and 'higher' is undefined once the counter wraps.
unambiguity.suggestion: Define the tie case (e.g. 'on equal counters the slot written last by convention, or slot 0') and either state the counter's width with a wrap-safe comparison or declare that it never wraps within the service life.

verifiability.reason: A test can seed the two slots with chosen counters and checksums and assert which value is returned, including the no-valid-slot report.

summary: Clean restore rule with the no-valid-slot case handled; the tie case and write-counter wrap-around are left undefined.
